title: AP Reported 16 Epstein-Related Files Missing; DOJ Later Restored One Photo After Review
description_medium: On Dec. 20, 2025, AP reported that at least 16 items had disappeared from DOJ’s public Epstein-files webpage less than a day after posting. The next day, DOJ restored a photograph showing Trump after reviewing it and finding no victim depicted. The status of the other items was not established in the reports reviewed.
description_long: The Associated Press reported on Dec. 20, 2025, that at least 16 items had disappeared from the Justice Department’s public Epstein-files webpage less than a day after they were posted. The items included photographs of paintings depicting nude women and a photograph showing Donald Trump, Jeffrey Epstein, Melania Trump and Ghislaine Maxwell. The next day, Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche said the photograph had been removed after prosecutors flagged it for review because of concerns about women pictured in it. DOJ said it restored the image unchanged after concluding there was no evidence that an Epstein victim appeared in it. The department said the review process was intended to protect victims. The removal and restoration document how the public webpage changed over two days, but the reporting does not establish who made each decision or the political motives behind it. Nor does the restoration of that photograph establish that all other removed items were reposted. The evidence supports a specific account of the public-file changes while leaving the status of the remaining items unresolved.

title: DOJ Restored a Trump Photograph to Its Epstein Files Page After a Victim-Privacy Review
description_medium: After AP reported at least 16 items missing from DOJ’s Epstein-files webpage, the department said it had temporarily removed the Trump photograph for review and restored it unchanged on Dec. 21, 2025, after finding no victim was depicted. Reports did not establish the final status of every other removed file.
description_long: The Justice Department’s public Epstein-files page was reported to have lost at least 16 items between Dec. 19 and 20, 2025. AP said the missing material included images and a photograph showing Donald Trump, Jeffrey Epstein, Melania Trump and Ghislaine Maxwell. On Dec. 21, DOJ restored the Trump photograph after a review found no evidence that an Epstein victim appeared in it. Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche said prosecutors had flagged the image because women appeared in it and the department wanted to assess possible privacy concerns. DOJ described the temporary removal as a precaution to protect victims. The reports establish that the image disappeared and was later reposted without alteration; they do not establish that it was removed because Trump appeared in it. They also do not demonstrate that all other missing items were restored or identify who directed each change. The incident is a documented episode in the release and review of Epstein-related records, while the status of the remaining items and the department’s decision chain remain unclear.
